#Again, My Hypothesis are:
H1: Attitudes toward gender equality differ significantly across gender groups.
  Categorical IV: Sex. Continuous DV: Gender equality composite Composite items: Gender_Equality_1, Gender_Equality_2, Gender_Equality_3.

H2: Individuals reporting greater romantic intimacy with their partners report higher relationship satisfaction.
  Continuous IV: Romantic intimacy composite. Continuous DV: Relationship satisfaction. Composite IV items: Love_1 through Love_5 DV items prqc_1 through prqc_3

## 1. Load the processed data

```{r load}
# Open the project's .Rproj file before running chunks.
# Install psych once in the Console if needed: install.packages("psych")

library(psych)
library(ggplot2)

h1Data <- read.csv("processed-data/H1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("processed-data/H2.csv")


```

## 2. Look at the distribution first

```{r histogram}
# A histogram groups numerical values into intervals (bins).
# Bar height shows how many observations fall in each interval.
# Start by looking at the distribution before calculating summary statistics.
# Add readable labels to the same histogram.

#H1
## Sex (categorical variable)

sex_bar <- ggplot(data = h1Data,
                     aes(x = Sex,
                     fill = Sex)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x="Sex Groups",
       y="Amount of People participated in the survey.\n (LOG Scale)",
       title="Histogram plot of responses of sex variable in LOG Scale") + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_y_log10()
sex_bar


genderEqHist <- ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = avgGenderEq)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Avg Gender Equality Score (1-7)", y = "Count",
       title = "Distribution of Gender Equality Scores")
genderEqHist


avgLoveIntimacy <- ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = avgLoveIntimacy)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Avg Intimacy Score (1-5)", y = "Count",
       title = "Distribution of Romantic Intimacy Scores")
avgLoveIntimacy


avgRelationshipSatis <- ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = avgPrqc)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Avg Relationship Satisfaction (1-7)", y = "Count",
       title = "Distribution of Relationship Satisfaction Scores")
avgRelationshipSatis



```

## 3. One statistic at a time

```{r individual_statistics}
# Mean: add the scores and divide by the number of observed responses.
mean(h1Data$avgGenderEq)
mean(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)
mean(h2Data$avgPrqc)

# Median: the middle score after sorting the responses.
median(h1Data$avgGenderEq)
median(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)
median(h2Data$avgPrqc)

# Table:counting how many people are in each sex group
table(h1Data$Sex)

# Range: return the minimum and maximum, rather than their difference.
range(h1Data$avgGenderEq)
range(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)
range(h2Data$avgPrqc)

# IQR: the 75th percentile minus the 25th percentile.
IQR(h1Data$avgGenderEq)
IQR(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)
IQR(h2Data$avgPrqc)


```

## 4. Standardize a variable

```{r standardize}

# Standardized scores have mean equal to 0 and standard deviation equals to 1.

#Standardize H1: Avg Gender Equality
h1Data$avgGenderEqStandardized <- as.numeric(scale(h1Data$avgGenderEq))

#Standardize H2: avg prqc
h2Data$avgPrqcStandardized <- as.numeric(scale(h2Data$avgPrqc))

#Standardize H2: avg love intimacy
h2Data$avgLoveIntimacyStandardized <- as.numeric(scale(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy))

```

```{r}

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = avgLoveIntimacyStandardized)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  labs(x = "Romantic Intimacy (z-score)", y = "Count",
       title = "Distribution of Standardized Romantic Intimacy Scores (standardized)")


```

## 5. Covariance and correlation

```{r association}
# Covariance describes whether two variables tend to move together.
# Positive: higher values tend to occur together. Negative: higher values tend to accompany lower values.
# Its size depends on the units and is not restricted to -1 through 1.

# Pearson correlation expresses a linear association on a -1 to 1 scale.


#Covariance for H2 
cov(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy, h2Data$avgPrqc, use = "complete.obs")

# Correlation for H2
cor(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy, h2Data$avgPrqc, use = "complete.obs")
## output: high correlation

#Correlation Matrix for H2
corData <- h2Data[, c("avgLoveIntimacy", "avgPrqc")]
cor(corData, use = "complete.obs")
```

## 6. Several statistics at once

```{r combined_summaries}
# summary() reports minimum, quartiles, median, mean, maximum, and missing counts when present.

# psych::describe() reports n, mean, SD, median, minimum, maximum, range width (max minus min), skewness, kurtosis, and other summaries.
# However it does not report every statistic above: compute IQR, cov(), and cor() separately.


summary(h1Data$avgGenderEq)
psych::describe(h1Data$avgGenderEq)

summary(h2Data$avgPrqc)
psych::describe(h2Data$avgPrqc)

summary(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)
psych::describe(h2Data$avgLoveIntimacy)

```


```{r  H1 stats by sex}
# aggregate() calculates statistics separately for each sex group

aggregate(avgGenderEq ~ Sex, data = h1Data, FUN = mean)
aggregate(avgGenderEq ~ Sex, data = h1Data, FUN = median)
aggregate(avgGenderEq ~ Sex, data = h1Data, FUN = sd)

```
